chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said:

Al-Kumayt chanted a poem for Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he said: 'May Allah make my desire sincere for me, so I do not drown the drawing [of the bow], and my arrows do not waver.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not say like this,
I do not drown the drawing
but say, 'So I have drowned the drawing
and my arrows do not waver'.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, title of Imam al-Sadiq

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the poetic correction given by Imam al-Sadiq to Al-Kumayt regarding the drawing of the bow?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, the poet Al-Kumayt recites to Imam al-Sadiq (AS), who corrects the grammatical aspect of the verb 'to drown' (gharaq) from the present tense to the perfect tense, shifting the meaning from a wish for future success to a declaration of completed certainty. This subtle linguistic refinement underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on precision in language as a reflection of spiritual and practical decisiveness, illustrating how minor syntactic changes can alter the theological weight of a statement. The correction highlights the Imam’s role not only as a spiritual guide but also as an authority on the nuances of Arabic rhetoric and meaning.
